claim: oncRNAs were defined as smRNA loci significantly present in cancer and absent in tumor-adjacent normal samples
quote: smRNA loci that were significantly present in cancer samples and absent in tumor-adjacent normal samples were annotated as oncRNAs

claim: 260,968 high-confidence oncRNAs were discovered across 32 cancer types
quote: we discovered 260,968 high-confidence oncRNAs that are specifically expressed in one or more cancers

claim: 15,827 oncRNAs were annotated in breast cancer (TCGA-BRCA)
quote: we annotated 15,827 oncRNAs in breast cancer (TCGA-BRCA)

claim: oncRNA barcode Jaccard similarity is higher within the same tissue of origin
quote: we found significantly higher similarity among samples from the same tissue of origin (TOO)

claim: Recursive feature elimination reduced 260,968 oncRNAs to 1,805 classifier features
quote: we used recursive feature elimination in a 5-fold cross validation setup to reduce the feature space (from 260,968 to 1,805 oncRNA features)

claim: XGBoost with 500 trees on 1,805 oncRNAs gave 90.9% test accuracy for tissue of origin
quote: we observed a strong performance with 90.9% accuracy

claim: Classifier errors were enriched for misclassification between different squamous cancers
quote: our model’s errors were enriched with misclassifications between different squamous cancers

claim: A cpm-trained analog model performed equally well as the binarized digital model
quote: We found that the model trained on cpm data performed equally well and picked up important oncRNA features with similar patterns of expression as the binary model

claim: The digital/analog equivalence means the barcode is robust to imprecise smRNA quantification
quote: suggests that oncRNAs provide a digital barcode of cancer cell identity that is robust to the challenges in precise quantification of smRNAs

claim: CPTAC validation used 938 tumors across six cancer types
quote: smRNA sequencing data from 938 tumors across six cancer types from the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC)

claim: 84.9% of the 260,968 annotated oncRNAs were detected in at least one CPTAC cancer sample
quote: we found that 84.9% of our 260,968 annotated oncRNAs were detected in at least one cancer sample

claim: The TCGA-trained model achieved 82.1% accuracy on CPTAC samples
quote: achieving an overall accuracy of 82.1%

claim: 58.9% of oncRNAs map to existing longer RNAs; 41.1% are intergenic
quote: suggests that 58.9% of oncRNAs may originate from existing longer RNAs

claim: 386 TCGA ATAC-seq samples were used to relate oncRNA expression to chromatin accessibility
quote: we used 386 assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) samples from TCGA

claim: 1,989 oncRNA loci showed significant positive accessibility association at 1% FDR
quote: of which 1,989 oncRNA loci showed statistically significant associations at an FDR of 1%

claim: The accessibility association is one-sided: no oncRNAs in closed chromatin loci
quote: this association is entirely one-sided and we did not observe any oncRNAs in loci with closed chromatin

claim: 1,204 (60.5%) significant oncRNA loci overlap MDA-MB-231 ATAC peaks; 577 (29%) show GRO-seq transcription
quote: We also observed active transcription of 577 (29%) of the significant oncRNA loci

claim: 1,006 of 15,827 breast oncRNAs and 1,198 of 57,632 CRC oncRNAs are subtype-associated
quote: 1,006 show significant subtype-specific patterns across the TCGA-BRCA cohort

claim: Breast subtype classifiers reached AUCs 0.83-0.99; colon CMS classifiers 0.73-0.94
quote: Breast cancer subtype classifiers achieved areas under the curve (AUCs) between 0.83 and 0.99; similarly, colon cancer CMS classifiers achieved AUCs ranging between 0.73

claim: Breast subtype models erred most between luminal A and luminal B
quote: we observed that the breast cancer models made a higher number of mistakes when distinguishing subgroups of luminal breast cancers

claim: Screens used four cell lines with xenograft models: MDA-MB-231, SW480, A549, C4-2B
quote: selected a human cell line with an established xenograft model for each cancer: MDA-MB-231 (breast), SW480 (colon), A549 (lung), and C4-2B (prostate)

claim: Loss-of-function used Tough Decoy constructs to sequester oncRNAs
quote: we generated a lentiviral library of Tough Decoys (TuDs) to sequester oncRNAs

claim: Gain-of-function screens nominated hits in breast and colon but not lung or prostate
quote: however, the lung and prostate cancer screens did not nominate any significant oncRNAs

claim: Roughly 5% of screened oncRNAs showed a significant tumor growth phenotype
quote: Between the gain- and loss-of-function screens, roughly 5% of oncRNAs showed a significant tumor growth phenotype.

claim: oncRNA.ch7.29 and oncRNA.ch17.67 map to 3'UTRs of SCRN1 and PSMD12
quote: map to the 3′ untranslated regions (UTRs) of cancer-associated genes, SCRN1 and PSMD12, respectively

claim: Both driver oncRNAs associate with poor clinical outcomes but not with stage or receptor subtype
quote: we did not find any significant associations when we stratified oncRNA expression by cancer stage or receptor subtype for either oncRNA

claim: oncRNA.ch7.29 associates with EMT upregulation; ch17.67 with DNA repair and E2F
quote: we observed a significant association between oncRNA.ch7.29 expression and upregulation of genes in the epithelial-mesenchymal transition

claim: Overexpression raised MDA-MB-231 primary tumor growth 2.6-fold (ch7.29) and 1.7-fold (ch17.67)
quote: increased the primary tumor growth rates of cells implanted in the mammary fat-pad of NOD scid gamma (NSG) mice by 2.6- and 1.7-fold, respectively, relative to scrambled controls

claim: Vimentin was upregulated in ch7.29-overexpressing HCC-LM2 and MDA-MB-231 cells
quote: we observed a significant upregulation of vimentin in both HCC-LM2 and MDA-MB-231 cell lines overexpressing oncRNA.ch7.29

claim: The E2F regulon was not significantly associated with ch17.67 in MDA-231 cells
quote: we note that the E2F target regulon was not shown to be significantly associated with oncRNA.ch17.67 in MDA-231 cells

claim: Cell-free profiling used 25 cancer cell lines spanning nine tissues of origin
quote: we selected 25 established human cancer cell lines representing nine TOOs

claim: About 0.5% of cfRNA reads were oncRNAs; ~30% of the pancancer list appeared in at least two cell lines
quote: Roughly 0.5% of cfRNA reads were annotated as oncRNAs in our pipeline, with about 30% of our pancancer list of oncRNAs detected in at least two cell lines

claim: Cell-free oncRNA profiles cluster cell lines by tissue of origin
quote: 2D UMAP and PCA visualizations of cell-free oncRNA profiles show clustering of cell lines by TOO

claim: The clinical study drew 1 mL serum samples from 267 I-SPY 2 breast cancer patients
quote: We extracted cfRNA from 1 mL serum samples from 267 breast cancer patients treated with standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) alone

claim: 192 of 267 patients had T0 and T3 samples passing QC; oncRNA burden is library-size-normalized sum across loci
quote: we measured total oncRNA burden, defined as the sum of all oncRNA species across all loci normalized by library size

claim: oncRNA burden fell significantly overall after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
quote: we observed a significant overall reduction in oncRNA burden after NAC

claim: Median follow-up was 4.72 years and high delta-oncRNA predicted poor overall and disease-free survival
quote: With a median follow-up of 4.72 years in our study

claim: Delta-oncRNA stays informative of survival in multivariable Cox models controlling for pCR or RCB
quote: we performed multivariable Cox regression analyses, and we observed that ΔoncRNA remains significantly informative of survival even when controlling for pCR or RCB

claim: The screen hit rate is called a conservative estimate for construct, context and model reasons
quote: we view these numbers of significant hits to be a conservative estimate due to several factors

claim: Xenografts lack adaptive immunity and native tumor microenvironment
quote: lacking key characteristics such as adaptive immunity and native tumor microenvironment

claim: Cancer cells actively secrete RNA whereas DNA is passively shed on cell death
quote: cancer cells actively secrete RNA, whereas DNA is passively shed because of cell death

claim: Circulating oncRNA detection needs no primary tumor profiling, giving a tumor-naive approach
quote: providing a tumor-naive approach to monitoring cancer

claim: The mechanism and biogenesis of the two driver oncRNAs remain unknown
quote: the molecular mechanism of action and biogenesis of oncRNA.ch7.29 and oncRNA.ch17.67 remain unknown
